question: Which finance minister of Mughal emperor Akbar introduced the system of taxation called 'Dahsala'?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Raja Todar Mal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__Raja Todar Mal was the finance minister of the Mughal emperor Akbar. 
 
• He introduced the Dahsala system of taxation in **1580 AD. **
 
• This system was based on the average production of different crops over the past 10 years. 
 
• The state's share was one-third of the average produce. 
 
• The Dahsala system was adopted in most of the provinces of the Mughal Empire, **except for the ones that were predominantly Muslim.**
 
• The Dahsala system was a **more efficient and equitable system of taxation** than the previous systems. 
 
• It helped to ensure that the state received a fair share of the revenue, while also protecting the interests of the farmers. 
 
• The Dahsala system was also one of the factors that **contributed to the economic prosperity** of the Mughal empire during Akbar's reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Raja Todar Mal divided all cultivable land into four categories:

 

 
• Polaj__: It was the best land cultivated every year.
 
• __Parauti__: It was the land of the second category which was left uncultivated for one year or two so that it could recover its fertility.
 
• __Chachar__: It was left uncultivated for three to four years in order to make it cultivable.
 
• __**Banjar:**__ Land that was not fit for agriculture and was mostly left uncultivated for a long time.
